title: New Development Bank
definition: The New Development Bank (NDB), formerly referred to as the BRICS Development Bank, is a multilateral development bank established by the BRICS states (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa) to mobilize resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in emerging economies and developing countries.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Civil Services Exam (Prelims: International financial institutions, voting rights, headquarters; Mains GS-2/GS-3: Global economic governance, reform of Bretton Woods institutions, India's role in multilateral groupings, and infrastructure financing).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of the New Development Bank.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of international economics and Bretton Woods institutions
